data.text: When a query returns many items, pagination lets clients fetch data in chunks. Hot Chocolate supports both offset-based and cursor-based pagination.
Offset pagination uses `skip` and `take` arguments. It's simple but can miss or duplicate items if data changes between pages.

data.title: Offset Pagination
data.content: Page through books with skip and take.

data.text: Cursor pagination uses a opaque cursor to mark the current position. It's more reliable for real-time data and is the Relay specification standard.

data.title: Cursor Pagination
Offset Query
Cursor Query
data.content: Get the next page using after cursor.

data.title: When to Use Which
data.text: Use offset pagination for simple admin panels. Use cursor pagination for mobile apps and infinite scroll where data changes frequently.

terms.definition: Pagination using skip/take or page number and page size.
Pagination using an opaque cursor that points to the next set of results.
Metadata about the current page, including hasNextPage and endCursor.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Offset pagination is simple but fragile
Cursor pagination handles real-time data better
